svg.title: Adam epsilon effect for small constant gradients
svg.desc: For a constant positive scalar gradient of magnitude c greater than zero, bias corrected first moment and root second moment both equal c. With epsilon zero the normalized update is one, while with epsilon point one it is c divided by c plus point one. Animated markers trace a parameter sweep, not training iterations.
svg.text: Constant positive gradient g = c · corrected moments
With eps > 0, positive gradient scaling is not exactly invariant.
